[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Technical Tutorial: Concatenation, Stacking, and Splitting in NumPy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Manipulating the shape and structure of arrays is a fundamental requirement in data science and numerical computing. NumPy provides robust utilities to join multiple arrays together or to divide a single array into multiple sub-arrays. This tutorial explores concatenation, stacking, and splitting operations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Array Concatenation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The np.concatenate() function is used to join a sequence of arrays along an existing axis. All arrays must have the same shape, except in the dimension corresponding to the axis along which they are being concatenated."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np

a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
b = np.array([[5, 6], [7, 8]])

# Concatenate along axis 0 (rows)
result_axis0 = np.concatenate((a, b), axis=0)
print("Concatenate axis 0:\n", result_axis0)

# Concatenate along axis 1 (columns)
result_axis1 = np.concatenate((a, b), axis=1)
print("Concatenate axis 1:\n", result_axis1)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Array Stacking"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"While concatenation joins arrays along an existing axis, stacking is essentially concatenation along a new axis. NumPy offers several convenient wrappers like np.vstack() (vertical stack), np.hstack() (horizontal stack), and np.dstack() (depth stack)."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"x = np.array([1, 2, 3])
y = np.array([4, 5, 6])

# Vertical stack (row-wise)
v_stacked = np.vstack((x, y))
print("Vertical Stack:\n", v_stacked)

# Horizontal stack (column-wise)
h_stacked = np.hstack((x, y))
print("Horizontal Stack:\n", h_stacked)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Array Splitting"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Conversely, splitting breaks an array into multiple sub-arrays. The primary functions for this operation are np.split(), np.hsplit(), and np.vsplit(). You can specify either the number of equal sections to return or a list of index positions where the split should occur."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"original = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60])

# Split into 3 equal sub-arrays
split_equal = np.split(original, 3)
print("Split into 3:", split_equal)

# Split at specific indices
split_custom = np.split(original, [2, 4])
print("Split at indices [2, 4]:", split_custom)"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use np.concatenate() when combining arrays along an already present axis."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use np.vstack() and np.hstack() for quick and readable 1D and 2D dimensional expansions."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use np.split() with index arrays to divide data dynamically based on conditional boundaries."}]
